/-- A simple operation: associative and returns one of its two arguments -/
structure SimpleOp where

def evalString (f : SimpleOp n) : List (Fin n) → Fin n
  | []      => panic! "empty string not allowed"

/-- A simple operation: associative and returns one of its two arguments -/
structure SimpleOp where
  op : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n
  assoc : ∀ x y z, op (op x y) z = op x (op y z)
  idem : ∀ x y, op x y = x ∨ op x y = y

/-- Left-associative evaluation of a string under a simple operation -/
def evalString (f : SimpleOp n) : List (Fin n) → Fin n
  | []      => panic! "empty string not allowed"
  | x :: xs => xs.foldl f.op x

/-- Two strings are equivalent if they evaluate the same under all simple operations -/
def equiv (x y : List (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : SimpleOp n, evalString n f x = evalString n f y

-- Reflexivity of equivalence: any string is equivalent to itself
theorem equiv_refl {n : ℕ} [Inhabited (Fin n)] : ∀ x : List (Fin n), equiv n x x :=
  fun x f => rfl

-- Symmetry of equivalence: if x ~ y, then y ~ x
theorem equiv_symm {n : ℕ} [Inhabited (Fin n)] : ∀ x y, equiv n x y → equiv n y x :=
  fun x y h f => (h f).symm

-- Transitivity of equivalence: if x ~ y and y ~ z, then x ~ z
theorem equiv_trans {n : ℕ} [Inhabited (Fin n)] : ∀ x y z, equiv n x y → equiv n y z → equiv n x z :=
  fun x y z h₁ h₂ f => (h₁ f).trans (h₂ f)

/-- Declaring this equivalence as a Setoid instance -/
def stringSetoid (n : ℕ) [Inhabited (Fin n)] : Setoid (List (Fin n)) :=
{
  r := @equiv n _,
  iseqv := ⟨equiv_refl, equiv_symm _ _, equiv_trans _ _ _⟩
}

/-- A string is full if it contains every variable at least once -/
def isFull (s : List (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Fin n, i ∈ s

/-- A double rainbow is a pair of full strings (permutations) -/
def DoubleRainbow := { p : List (Fin n) × List (Fin n) //
  p.1.Nodup ∧ p.2.Nodup ∧ ∀ i, i ∈ p.1 ∧ i ∈ p.2 }

  d.val.1 ++ d.val.2

/-- The quotient type of strings under simple equivalence -/
noncomputable def StringClass : Type := Quotient (stringSetoid n)

/-- All permutations of `Fin n` (i.e., all full strings with no repetition) -/
def allPerms : Finset (List (Fin n)) :=
  (List.permutations (List.finRange n)).toFinset

  For every pair of permutations of Fin n, concatenate them,
  then take their equivalence class under `equiv`. These are called double rainbows.
-/

  |>.image (λ ⟨a, b⟩ => Quotient.mk (stringSetoid n) (a ++ b))
